'''Victor Vâlcovici''' ({{OldStyleDate|21 September|1885|9 September}} &ndash; 21 June 1970) was a [[Romania]]n mechanician and mathematician.

==Biography==
Born into a modest family in [[Galați]], he graduated first in his class in 1904 from [[Nicolae Bălcescu National College|Nicolae Bălcescu High School]] in [[Brăila]]. Entering the [[University of Bucharest]] on a scholarship, he attended its faculty of sciences, where he had as teachers [[Spiru Haret]] and [[Gheorghe Țițeica]].<ref name="VL">{{cite web|url=https://www.viata-libera.ro/diaspora/42453-galati-viata-libera-galateni-care-au-uimit-lumea-victor-valcovici|title=Gălățeni care au uimit lumea – Victor Vâlcovici|first=D.C.|last=Predescu| language=ro|newspaper=[[Viața Liberă]] |date=May 23, 2013|access-date=February 16, 2022}}</ref> After graduating in 1907 with a degree in mathematics, he taught high school for two years before leaving for [[University of Göttingen]] on another scholarship to pursue a doctorate in mathematics. He wrote his thesis  under the direction of [[Ludwig Prandtl]] and defended it in 1913; the thesis, titled ''Ueber die diskontinuierliche Flussigkeitsbewegungen mit zwei freien Strahlen'' (Discontinuous flow of liquids in two free dimensions),<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=248030}}</ref><ref>Otlăcan, pp. 125–6</ref><ref>{{citation|first=Victor|last=Vâlcovici|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/007898486|title=Über diskontinuierliche Flüssigkeitsbewegungen mit zwei freien Strahlen|language=de|year=1913|publisher=Dieterich|location=Göttingen|jfm=44.0859.01}}</ref> amplified upon the work of [[Bernhard Riemann]].<ref name="h1361"/>

He was subsequently named assistant professor of mechanics at the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]], rising to full professor in 1918.<ref name="o127">Otlăcan, p. 127</ref> In 1921, he became rector of the [[Politehnica University of Timișoara|Polytechnic School of Timișoara]]. There, he was also professor of rational mechanics and founded a laboratory dedicated to the field.<ref name="h1361"/> During his nine years as rector, he worked to place the recently founded university on a solid foundation.<ref name="o127"/> From 1930 until retiring in 1962, he taught experimental mechanics at the University of Bucharest.<ref name="h1361"/> In the government of [[Nicolae Iorga]], he served as [[Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure|Minister of Public Works]] from 1931 to 1932. During this time, he introduced a modern road network that featured paved highways.<ref name="h1361">Hager, p. 1361</ref><ref name="o127"/> In 1936 he gave an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Oslo]], with title ''Sur le sillage derrière un obstacle circulaire'' (In the wake of a circular obstacle).<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1936.2/ICM1936.2.ocr.pdf|title=Comptes rendus du Congrès International des Mathématiciens: Oslo, 14–18 julliet 1936|location=Oslo|publisher=[[Anton Wilhelm Brøgger (printer)|A.W. Brøggers]]|year=1937|page=250|oclc=1404131}}</ref>

Elected a corresponding [[list of members of the Romanian Academy|member of the Romanian Academy]] in 1936,<ref>Otlăcan, p. 126, 127</ref> he was [[List of purged members of the Romanian Academy|stripped of his membership]] by the new [[Communist Romania|communist regime]] in 1948,<ref>{{cite journal|first=Păun Ion|last=Otiman|author-link=Păun Otiman|url=http://www.akademos.asm.md/files/1948_anul%20imensei%20jertfe%20a%20Academiei%20romane.pdf|title=1948–Anul imensei jertfe a Academiei Române|language=ro|journal=Akademos|volume=4|issue=31|date=December 2013|pages=115–124|archive-date=2020-07-14|access-date=2015-03-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714065421/http://www.akademos.asm.md/files/1948_anul%20imensei%20jertfe%20a%20Academiei%20romane.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{Rp|123}} but made a titular member of the [[Romanian Academy]] in 1965.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acad.ro/bdar/armembriLit.php?vidT=V|title= Membrii Academiei Române din 1866 până în prezent|language=ro|publisher=[[Romanian Academy]]}}</ref> His numerous articles on theoretical and applied mechanics covered topics such as the principles of variational mechanics, the mechanics of ideal fluid flow, the theory of elasticity and astronomy.<ref name="h1361"/>

He died in 1970 in [[Bucharest]], and was buried in the city's [[Bellu Cemetery]]. Streets have been named after Victor Vâlcovici in [[Brăila]], [[Galați]], and [[Timișoara]]; a school in Galați also bears his name.
